intro: Searching for an asbestos surveyor near you usually means you need to know whether asbestos is present in a building before you buy, sell, refurbish or manage it. You want someone local who can carry out the right kind of survey and give you a clear report, without the guesswork. iComply introduces you to a suitable UK asbestos surveyor who will quote you directly.
need_heading: What people searching for an asbestos surveyor near me usually need
need_lead: Most people are at a point where a property transaction, refurbishment or ongoing duty to manage asbestos means they need a proper survey rather than a quick look.
needs: You are buying or selling a property and need to know whether asbestos-containing materials are present before exchange.
You are planning building works and need a refurbishment and demolition survey to identify asbestos before anyone disturbs the fabric of the building.
You are a duty holder for non-domestic premises and need a management survey to help you manage asbestos in the building.
You have found a material you suspect contains asbestos and want a surveyor to confirm what it is and what to do next.
You need a surveyor who can attend a site near you and produce a report that other trades and professionals can rely on.
context_heading: Why UKAS accreditation matters for asbestos surveying
context: Asbestos surveying is specialist work, and the recognised mark of competence for organisations carrying out asbestos surveys is accreditation by UKAS. Asking whether the organisation is UKAS-accredited for surveying is a straightforward way to check that the work will be done to a recognised standard. Many surveyors are also members of RICS, which sets professional standards for firms it regulates.

There are different types of asbestos survey, and the right one depends on your situation. A management survey is typically for premises that are in use, while a refurbishment and demolition survey is needed before works that will disturb the building. Make sure you know which report type you are being offered before you commission the work.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Tell us the type of property and roughly when it was built, as asbestos is more common in buildings from certain periods.
Explain why you need the survey, such as a property purchase, planned refurbishment or managing a non-domestic building.
Let us know whether you need a management survey or a refurbishment and demolition survey, if you already know.
Give the location of the property so we can introduce you to a surveyor who covers your area.
Mention any materials you are particularly concerned about, such as textured coatings, insulation or cement sheeting.
Tell us whether you are the owner, buyer, tenant or duty holder, as this affects what the surveyor will need from you.
questions_heading: Questions to ask the asbestos surveyor
questions: Is your organisation accredited by UKAS for asbestos surveying?
Which type of survey will you carry out, and what will the report include?
Will you take samples for laboratory analysis, and is that included in your quote?
How will you access any areas that are difficult to reach, such as roof voids or sealed spaces?
What experience do you have with buildings like mine and the materials I am concerned about?
What happens if asbestos is found during the survey?

faqs.q: Do I need an asbestos survey before I refurbish my property?
faqs.a: A refurbishment and demolition survey is normally needed before works that will disturb the building fabric, so that asbestos can be identified and dealt with safely. The surveyor will advise on the right type of survey for your project.

faqs.q: How do I check that an asbestos surveyor is properly qualified?
faqs.a: Look for organisations accredited by UKAS for asbestos surveying, and ask whether the surveyor is a member of a professional body such as RICS. You can also ask to see examples of similar work they have done.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a management survey and a refurbishment survey?
faqs.a: A management survey is typically for premises in normal use and helps duty holders manage asbestos, while a refurbishment and demolition survey is more intrusive and is carried out before works that will disturb the building. The right choice depends on your plans.
